applicability: Continuous admission, mixed prefill/decode and final drain
Recorded Drama3 B300 C64 diagnostic only

findings.direction: Use the whole-run mean batch as sustained-admission occupancy
findings.reason: A whole-run mean can be dominated by drain. In the recorded C64 diagnostic, pure decode averaged 60.718 of 64 active requests during client admission, final drain averaged 8.793, and the whole-trace pure-decode average was 28.146
findings.revisit_when: Separate the client-admission and drain intervals before reading occupancy; using the whole-run mean can misidentify scheduling headroom

findings.direction: Read a near-full batch in a selected interval as a service speedup
findings.reason: A near-full batch in a selected interval does not establish a service speedup; client in-flight counts also include queueing and codec work, and CPU/GPU clock alignment was approximate
findings.revisit_when: Keep all requests and complete quality/repetition groups in the end-to-end metric rather than a selected-phase rate

findings.direction: Count PIECEWISE graph fragments instead of scheduler annotations
findings.reason: The original investigation counted scheduler execution annotations rather than PIECEWISE graph fragments, and retained the full request cohort for acceptance. Scheduled prompt entries may be chunks, not unique requests
findings.revisit_when: Confirm which quantity the annotations represent; kernel sums, annotation unions and SM utilization are different quantities

limitations: No new measurement or trace reproduction
Selected-phase occupancy is not service throughput
Raw evidence remains under its existing owner
attribution: InferRSI issue #10 diagnostic evidence; extraction retains the original observation and its limits
